qt: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE) Subject:

The latest FAO figures show that affordable healthy eating continues to be a challenge: the price of a healthy diet in Europe went up by 36 % between 2021 and 2025. That is compared to a world average of around 25 %1. This situation calls into question the implementation of the Farm to Fork Strategy. One of the strategy’s aims was to propose harmonised mandatory front-of-pack nutrition labelling. However, the future publication of such a legislative proposal remains uncertain, as does the achievement of other binding and non-binding targets. 1.

Does the Commission intend to revise or update the Farm to Fork Strategy in the light of geopolitical developments, food security and the new competitiveness agenda for agriculture and the agri-food sector?
What concrete measures does the Commission intend to take to improve the affordability of healthy and nutritious food, while ensuring that Europe’s farmers and agri-food industry remain competitive?

Which of the legislative initiatives announced in the Farm to Fork Strategy but not yet presented will be put forward during the current mandate and what is the estimated timeline for these, including for front-of-pack nutrition labelling?
